title: Clamp `podman exec` oom_score_adj when it's too low
body:
When starting a container in rootless mode, if `oom_score_adj` is set to a value that is lower than Podman's own `oom_score_adj`, [we clamp it before passing it to `crun`](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/392fbda7967cbbfd45cf02e21be5d6ba5a1841db/libpod/container_internal_common.go#L848) (which would fail otherwise).

This is particularly important when podman runs as a service (and has `oom_score_adj` set to `200`) and the container is created using the compatibility API (the container `oom_score_adj` is always set to zero).

The problem is that we haven't clamped `oom_score_adj` when exec'ing in a container. And `crun`, [which recently introduced the `oom_score_adj` support for `exec`](https://github.com/containers/crun/commit/499c3eb0c3), was failing:

```
write to `/proc/self/oom_score_adj`: Permission denied: OCI permission denied
```

This PR fixes this problem by clamping `oom_score_adj` on container exec too.

Note: the `crun` commit that triggers this problem hasn't been released yet, so the users who may have seen this are very limited. But we should release this Podman fix before a `crun` release to prevent the problem from spreading further.

comments.body: @l0rd @Luap99 I think this deserves backports to supported versions, or we'll keep getting issues like https://github.com/containers/crun/issues/2466

I agree the crun fix seem correct, we make the backports for 5.8/6.2. And users affected can just downgrade crun temporarily until the new podman release lands. I think you should just close the crun issues as wontfix.
